title: What Does "Sooner" Mean? The 1889 Land Run and OU's Nickname
question: What does Sooner mean and why are the Oklahoma football teams called the Sooners?
answer: A "Sooner" was a settler who slipped into Oklahoma's Unassigned Lands before the legal start of the April 22, 1889 Land Run. OU's teams took the Sooners nickname in 1908 after about a decade as the Rough Riders or Boomers.
summary: A Sooner jumped the gun in the April 22, 1889 Land Run. Learn how the term became OU's team nickname in 1908 after years as the Rough Riders and Boomers.
body: Every Sooner fan eventually gets asked what the nickname actually means, and the answer starts at noon on April 22, 1889. That was the opening of the Unassigned Lands, a roughly two-million-acre region in what became central Oklahoma. An estimated 50,000 people gathered around the boundaries, and signals ranging from pistol shots to a cannon at Fort Reno started the race for claims.

Two groups gave the story its famous words. Boomers were the pioneers who had campaigned for years to open the Unassigned Lands to settlement, and on run day big crowds massed at Kansas border towns such as Arkansas City and Caldwell. Sooners were the ones who got in early, entering ahead of time and hiding out until the legal moment so they could grab the best spots. An estimated 11,000 agricultural homesteads were claimed in that first run.

Over time the word lost its sting. As the university's own telling puts it, the energy of the pioneers and their descendants turned Sooner into shorthand for energetic, can-do people. OU also acknowledges the more complicated history underneath the Land Runs: the Unassigned Lands came from territory some tribal nations lost in Indian Territory under treaties renegotiated after the Civil War.

On the athletic side, OU teams went by Rough Riders or Boomers for about ten years before the Sooner nickname emerged in 1908. Both halves of the old story live on today: the Schooner's ponies are named Boomer and Sooner, and the fight song repeats both words over and over. By the 1920s, Oklahoma itself had become widely known as the Sooner State.
